messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] RmaPlm Error in .subset2(groups, 1) : subscript out of bounds
parts:
Hi,

your CDF is most likely corrupt. You didn't tell us what

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("HTHGU133A_Hs_ENTREZG");
print(cdf);

outputs, and also not how you obtained that CDF. However, it looks
like (it originates from) a custom CDF by the BrainArray project
[http://brainarray.mbni.med.umich.edu/]. Some of their releases have
invalid CDF headers, cf. thread '[customcdf] ENTREZG, AUGUSTUST for
pig species is updated' on May 8, 2012 [http://goo.gl/Xg1pp]. Also,
if you've used one of their invalid versions, you should have gotten
an error message when you tried to convert it to a binary CDF.

I've checked, the v1.16.0 release of HTHGU133A_Hs_ENTREZG.cdf *is
valid* - try that instead.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.author: b7f7a39f9f271360
messages.subject: Re: RmaPlm Error in .subset2(groups, 1) : subscript out of bounds
parts:
Hey,

thanks for fast help.

Yes, the cdf was downloaded from brainarray project, cdf version 16 from here:

http://brainarray.mbni.med.umich.edu/Brainarray/Database/CustomCDF/16.0.0/entrezg.asp

I didn't think cdf is corrupted since there was no error while converting the cdf to binary format.

So what I did, is that I have downloaded the same cdf once again, removed results from background correction and quantile normalization (left the rawData and annotation Data folders only)  and performed the script once again. It is running already over one week and still going, so this error which was the problem didn't occur.

Still don't know what was the problem, but it's ok now.

Thanks once again,
Marcin
